variants.headline: Party names a new leader
variants.sub: Leadership of {party} has changed, with {new} the new leader.
variants.body:
The party {party} has a new leader: {new}. A change at the head of an organisation is a political fact; a change in its programme is a separate question. Readers considering {target} should not have to accept the second as a necessary consequence of the first.

Management readers understand that a change in leadership is not a complete strategy document. The same restraint is useful in politics. A new party head does not establish a tax proposal or an economic policy, and decisions should not be anticipated as facts merely because the spokesperson has changed.

We are not persuaded by {target}. A change of leadership should not be allowed to turn political scrutiny into a courtesy exercise; public trust requires more than a place at the head of a party. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
